label: Q04
question: Is Date_Time_Local_ Pacific clock time with daylight saving (PST in winter, PDT in summer), or Pacific standard time all year? The CountCOFI manual calls the logger's time 'PST'.
context: Needed to build datetime_start_utc; also used by the cruise track match. First render (2026-09-27): every sighting and effort start falls in daylight when read as Pacific clock time (05:00-19:00), so the times are local, not UTC. Whether daylight saving was applied looks cruise-dependent: on many DST-season surveys before 2015 effort starts about an hour before PDT sunrise, as it would if the clock stayed on PST. Checked 2026-09-27: EDI 262.2 has a 'GMT Diff' per row, and most cruises kept Pacific standard time (UTC-8) all year, even in summer; only CC0607, CC0707, CC1008, CC1207, CC1304 and CC1507 used PDT. Reading them all as America/Los_Angeles had put 1,529 sightings (and their effort) an hour early; the ingest now applies the recorded offsets (cruise_utc_offset.csv). The sunrise check agrees with EDI on 21 of 22 summer cruises and suggests CC1104 and CC1407 also ran on UTC-8, while 2016+ summer cruises look like PDT. The lab's 2026-11-13 data dictionary says 'Local date and time'; its CountCOFI manual (the logger used from about 2016) says the logger's date and time are 'PST'. If that means UTC-8 all year (no daylight saving), the 2016-2025 summer cruises would move one hour later than the ingest now reads them.
proposed_answer: Local Pacific clock time, converted with each cruise's own GMT offset where EDI 262.2 records it (41 cruises, 2005-2015: 35 at UTC-8, 6 at UTC-7), else America/Los_Angeles with daylight saving. Please confirm the offset for the cruises EDI does not cover (2004, CC1104, CC1407, 2016-2022).
